- [comparable-observed-hand-structure] Organize the user's requested hand views so that alignment, structural layers, and purposeful drawing marks jointly clarify rather than overstate the observation.

scope.description: An optional comparative drawing-sheet direction for user-requested hand anatomy studies. It places distinct surface and skeletal views of the same hand in a shared analytical layout, aligning their wrist and joint axes where useful. Fine directional marks clarify observed structure while open paper keeps the views separate. It is a drawing-study mode, not medical instruction or a template of any historical sheet.
limitations: Use only for a user-requested hand or wrist anatomy study with multiple views or structural layers.
Preserve the requested laterality, view count, pose, framing, and annotation preference.
Distinguish surface form from skeletal study through separate views unless the user requests an overlay.
Do not add medical labels, diagnoses, or anatomical claims the user did not request.
Do not copy a named historical drawing or its page layout.

rules.applies_when: The user requests multiple views or layers of the same hand or wrist.
rules.instruction: Arrange only the requested views as a comparative sheet; relate wrist entry points, palm axes, and joint positions with consistent orientation or scale where appropriate, while keeping each view distinct.
rules.observable: A viewer can compare the requested views as belonging to the same hand without confusing surface and skeletal structure.
rules.reject_when: Views contradict the requested laterality or count, drift into unrelated poses, or overlap until their structures become ambiguous.
rules.avoid: copied page layouts, arbitrary view rotation, and unrequested extra studies

rules.applies_when: The request includes both an external hand view and internal or skeletal information.
rules.instruction: Keep surface contours, tendon or joint landmarks, and bones legible as separate analytical information; use adjacent views or restrained construction guides rather than implying unsupported transparency.
rules.observable: Surface and deeper structure can be distinguished, and the page does not confuse illustration with a medical explanation.
rules.reject_when: Bones are drawn through intact skin without a requested cutaway, landmarks contradict the requested view, or labels imply unsupported anatomy.
rules.avoid: invented anatomy, false transparency, medical diagnosis, and pseudo-labels

rules.applies_when: The user requests a drawing or study-sheet treatment on paper.
rules.instruction: Use light exploratory contours before selective darker structural lines; keep parallel hatching aligned with the turning plane and reserve the darkest marks for clear overlaps or joints.
rules.observable: Marks describe structure and observation, while open paper separates views and keeps the sheet readable.
rules.reject_when: Hatching becomes uniform decoration, construction lines obscure anatomy, or paper is filled with unrelated notes.
rules.avoid: uniform crosshatching, decorative page borders, and unrequested writing

joint_checks.instruction: Organize the user's requested hand views so that alignment, structural layers, and purposeful drawing marks jointly clarify rather than overstate the observation.
joint_checks.observable: The page reads as a comparative drawing study, with distinct views, clear surface-to-bone separation, and open paper intervals.
